name: arith_perfect_dvd_perfect_eq
statement: (m n : ℕ) (hm : m.Perfect) (hn : n.Perfect) (h : m ∣ n) : m = n
closed: ∀ (m n : ℕ) (hm : m.Perfect) (hn : n.Perfect) (h : m ∣ n), m = n
informal: A perfect number never properly divides another perfect number — write n = k·m; k = 0 is impossible, k = 1 gives equality, and for k > 1 Uses Mathlib2.ab_perfect_mul_abundant at the key step: k·m is abundant, contradicting perfection of n (Nat.Perfect excludes Abundant).
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), m.Perfect → n.Perfect → m ∣ n → m = n
